messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: unit testing memory leaks?
parts:
Is there any way to unit test a memory leak?

I have a test for softmax, that if I let it run for
a minute or two clearly shows the leak in 2.1.0
in the process monitor as growing memory usage for
the test.

I also have a hotfix for 2.1.1 that plugs the leak (just
a matter of switching operator new to a direct use of
memalloc_). It doesn't show the memory growth in the
process monitor.

But I don't know how to automate the test. Clearly if
I let it run 15 minutes it'd blow out memory, but that
seems a sub-optimal strategy.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: unit testing memory leaks?
parts:
On Sunday, December 29, 2013 9:27:50 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Is there any way to unit test a memory leak?

On !Windows, you can set the maximum amount of memory a process is allowed to have via

ulimit -v

which will fail quickly in the case of a memory leak. But I don't know how to do the equivalent thing on Windows.

Ben
